title: Terraform IaC: AWS VPC from Scratch
description: Build a production-grade AWS VPC with public/private subnets, NAT gateway, and route tables using Terraform.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Provision a complete AWS Virtual Private Cloud infrastructure using Terraform. You will create a multi-AZ VPC with public and private subnets, internet gateway, NAT gateway, and proper routing tables — all defined as Infrastructure as Code.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Terraform 1.6+ installed
- AWS CLI configured with lab credentials (us-east-1)
- Pre-installed: terraform-docs, tflint
- Working directory: /opt/terraform-vpc

### Tasks
1. Initialize a new Terraform project with proper backend configuration
2. Define a VPC with CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16 and enable DNS support
3. Create 2 public subnets across different availability zones
4. Create 2 private subnets across different availability zones
5. Deploy an Internet Gateway and attach it to the VPC
6. Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet for private subnet outbound traffic
7. Configure route tables for both public and private subnets
8. Output the VPC ID, subnet IDs, and NAT gateway public IP

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with AWS credentials pre-configured
- Terraform state stored locally (no S3 backend for lab)
- Destroy all resources after verification to avoid charges
tasks: Initialize a new Terraform project with proper backend configuration
Define a VPC with CIDR block 10.0.0.0/16 and enable DNS support
Create 2 public subnets across different availability zones
Create 2 private subnets across different availability zones
Deploy an Internet Gateway and attach it to the VPC
Deploy a NAT Gateway in a public subnet for private subnet outbound traffic
Configure route tables for both public and private subnets
Output the VPC ID, subnet IDs, and NAT gateway public IP

title: K3s Kubernetes Cluster on Ubuntu
description: Deploy a lightweight K3s Kubernetes cluster and deploy a multi-tier application with Ingress.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Install and configure a production-ready K3s Kubernetes cluster. Deploy a web application with a backend API, database, and Ingress controller. Verify all components are running correctly.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with root access
- K3s installer available at https://get.k3s.io
- kubectl pre-installed
- Working directory: /opt/k3s-lab

### Tasks
1. Install K3s with disabled Traefik (we will install NGINX Ingress manually)
2. Verify all nodes are in Ready state
3. Deploy a PostgreSQL database using a StatefulSet with PersistentVolumeClaim
4. Deploy a Node.js API backend as a Deployment with 3 replicas
5. Deploy a React frontend as a Deployment with 2 replicas
6. Create a Service for the API backend (ClusterIP) and frontend (NodePort)
7. Install NGINX Ingress Controller via Helm chart
8. Create an Ingress resource routing /api to the backend and / to the frontend

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- K3s kubeconfig at /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml
- Helm 3 pre-installed for Ingress controller installation

Deploy a Node.js API backend as a Deployment with 3 replicas
Deploy a React frontend as a Deployment with 2 replicas
Create a Service for the API backend (ClusterIP) and frontend (NodePort)
Install NGINX Ingress Controller via Helm chart
Create an Ingress resource routing /api to the backend and / to the frontend

title: AWS S3 Static Website with CloudFront CDN
description: Host a static website on S3 with CloudFront distribution, OAC, and custom error pages.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Deploy a static website to S3 and distribute it globally using CloudFront CDN. Configure Origin Access Control, custom error responses, and cache invalidation.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with AWS CLI and Terraform
- S3 bucket name must be globally unique (use your initials + random)
- AWS credentials pre-configured
- Working directory: /opt/s3-cloudfront

### Tasks
1. Create an S3 bucket with public access blocked
2. Upload static website files (index.html, error.html, styles.css) to S3
3. Configure S3 bucket policy to allow CloudFront OAC access
4. Create a CloudFront distribution with S3 as origin
5. Set custom error pages (404 → /error.html with 200 response)
6. Configure cache policy with 1-hour default TTL
7. Create a CloudFront invalidation for /index.html
8. Output the CloudFront distribution domain name

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root
- AWS credentials with S3 and CloudFront permissions
- Bucket naming: lab-static-site-{your-initials}-{random}

title: Docker Compose Multi-Service Stack
description: Deploy a full-stack application using Docker Compose with PostgreSQL, Redis, Node.js API, and Nginx reverse proxy.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Orchestrate a multi-container application stack using Docker Compose. The stack includes a PostgreSQL database, Redis cache, Node.js API server, and Nginx reverse proxy with proper networking, volumes, and health checks.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Docker and Docker Compose v2
- Available images: postgres:15-alpine, redis:7-alpine, node:20-alpine, nginx:1.27-alpine
- Working directory: /opt/docker-stack

### Tasks
1. Create a docker-compose.yml with all four services defined
2. Configure PostgreSQL with health check, persistent volume, and environment variables
3. Configure Redis with health check and command-line password protection
4. Build and run a Node.js API that connects to PostgreSQL and Redis
5. Configure Nginx as reverse proxy forwarding /api to Node.js service
6. Set up Docker networks so services communicate by service name
7. Configure named volumes for PostgreSQL data persistence
8. Deploy the full stack and verify all containers are healthy

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with Docker socket mounted
- All configuration files in /opt/docker-stack/
- Use 'docker compose' (v2 syntax, not docker-compose)

Configure PostgreSQL with health check, persistent volume, and environment variables
Configure Redis with health check and command-line password protection
Build and run a Node.js API that connects to PostgreSQL and Redis
Configure Nginx as reverse proxy forwarding /api to Node.js service
Set up Docker networks so services communicate by service name
Configure named volumes for PostgreSQL data persistence
Deploy the full stack and verify all containers are healthy

title: Azure DevOps CI/CD Pipeline with Docker
description: Set up a complete CI/CD pipeline using Docker that builds, tests, and deploys a Node.js application.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Configure a full CI/CD pipeline using Docker containers that builds a Node.js application, runs tests, performs security scanning, and deploys to a staging environment. All stages use Docker for consistency.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Docker and Docker Compose
- Node.js 20 available inside containers
- Pre-created Git repository at /opt/cicd-app
- Working directory: /opt/cicd-pipeline

### Tasks
1. Create a Dockerfile for multi-stage Node.js build (build + production)
2. Write a docker-compose.test.yml for running Jest tests in a container
3. Create a CI pipeline script (ci.sh) that runs lint, test, and build stages
4. Create a Dockerfile for the production image with non-root user
5. Write a deploy.sh script that stops old containers and deploys new ones
6. Set up health check endpoints in the Node.js application
7. Create a .dockerignore file to exclude unnecessary files
8. Run the full pipeline end-to-end and verify the app is accessible

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with Docker socket
- Application source at /opt/cicd-app/
- Pipeline scripts at /opt/cicd-pipeline/

title: Prometheus + Grafana Monitoring Stack
description: Deploy a complete monitoring solution with Prometheus scraping metrics and Grafana dashboards.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Set up a production-grade monitoring stack using Docker Compose. Prometheus will scrape system and application metrics, and Grafana will visualize them with pre-configured dashboards.

8. Verify both services are accessible and data is flowing

- Prometheus UI: localhost:9090
- Grafana UI: localhost:3000 (admin/monitoring-2024!)

title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling Group with ALB
description: Configure an Auto Scaling Group with Application Load Balancer for a high-availability web application.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Design and deploy an Auto Scaling Group backed by an Application Load Balancer. Configure launch templates, scaling policies, and health checks for a fault-tolerant web application.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Terraform and AWS CLI
- AWS credentials with EC2, ELB, and AutoScaling permissions
- Pre-created VPC with 2 public subnets
- Working directory: /opt/asg-alb

### Tasks
1. Create a Launch Template with user data that installs and starts nginx
2. Configure an Auto Scaling Group with min=1, max=4, desired=2
3. Deploy an Application Load Balancer with target group
4. Create a health check for the target group on port 80
5. Configure a scaling policy based on CPU utilization (target 70%)
6. Create a security group allowing inbound HTTP from ALB only
7. Verify instances are registered with the target group
8. Test load distribution by making multiple HTTP requests

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with AWS credentials
- VPC and subnets pre-provisioned in us-east-1
- Use terraform for all infrastructure

title: GCP Cloud Run Serverless Deployment
description: Deploy a containerized application to Google Cloud Run with auto-scaling and traffic splitting.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Deploy a Python Flask application to Google Cloud Run as a serverless container. Configure auto-scaling, traffic splitting between revisions, and custom domain mapping.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with gcloud CLI pre-installed
- GCP project with Cloud Run API enabled
- Docker installed for building images
- Working directory: /opt/cloudrun-deploy

### Tasks
1. Create a Dockerfile for the Python Flask application
2. Build the Docker image locally
3. Configure gcloud with the provided project credentials
4. Deploy to Cloud Run with 100% traffic to the initial revision
5. Make code changes and deploy as a new revision with 50/50 traffic split
6. Configure Cloud Run service with minimum 1 and maximum 10 instances
7. Set environment variables for DATABASE_URL and API_KEY
8. Verify the service URL is accessible and returns HTTP 200

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with gcloud credentials
- GCP project: lab-cloudrun-project
- Region: us-central1
- Auth: service account with Cloud Run Admin role

title: Kubernetes Persistent Volumes with StatefulSet
description: Deploy a stateful application on Kubernetes using StatefulSets, PersistentVolumeClaims, and headless Services.
briefing:

- K3s pre-installed with local-path storage class

title: AWS Lambda Serverless API with API Gateway

briefing:

2. Create Lambda function for creating tasks (POST /tasks)
3. Create Lambda function for listing tasks (GET /tasks)
4. Create Lambda function for getting a single task (GET /tasks/{id})
5. Create Lambda function for deleting a task (DELETE /tasks/{id})
6. Deploy API Gateway REST API with proper resource paths
7. Configure CORS headers for browser access
8. Test all endpoints and verify DynamoDB contains the data

### Permissions & Access
- Container runs as root with AWS credentials
- Region: us-east-1
- Lambda zip files pre-packaged in /opt/serverless-api/lambdas/

title: AWS SQS and SNS Event-Driven Architecture
description: Build a decoupled microservices architecture using SQS queues, SNS topics, and Lambda processors.
briefing:
### Mission Objective
Design an event-driven architecture where an SNS topic fans out messages to multiple SQS queues. Each queue is consumed by a dedicated Lambda function. Implement dead-letter queues for failed processing.

### Environment
- Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with Terraform and AWS CLI
- Python 3.12 Lambda runtime
- AWS credentials with SQS, SNS, and Lambda access
- Working directory: /opt/sqs-sns-arch

### Tasks
1. Create an SNS topic for incoming orders
2. Create 3 SQS queues: orders-processing, orders-notifications, orders-analytics
3. Subscribe all 3 queues to the SNS topic (fan-out pattern)
4. Create dead-letter queues for each processing queue
5. Create 3 Lambda functions, each consuming from one queue
